issues.detail: The Hebrew 'שִׁוִּיתִי' (I set/placed) is rendered as 'Tôi nín lặng' (I was silent), which is not the meaning of the verb; the Hebrew does not mention silence here.

The Hebrew 'כֵּן יְשַׁבֵּר כָּל עַצְמוֹתָי' means 'so He breaks all my bones' (with 'כֵּן' = 'so/thus'), but the Vietnamese 'như thể Ngài bẻ gãy mọi xương tôi như sư tử vậy' adds 'như sư tử' (like a lion) and reorders the simile, making it seem the breaking is like a lion's action, whereas the Hebrew compares the 'setting' (or the state) to a lion, not the breaking.
The Vietnamese adds 'nín lặng' (silent) which has no basis in the Hebrew text.
